corpusSummary: This corpus comprises 60+ social-science studies (2026) examining how large language models and generative AI influence trust, decision making, education, health communication, and policy research. Across domains, papers analyze user experience, adoption, and embodiment; probe AI as a research tool, analysis collaborator, and design partner; assess risks around misinformation, bias, ethics, and governance; and highlight opportunities for pedagogy, literacy, and data-driven decision support while calling for validation and responsible use.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Across health, education, and everyday contexts, studies explore trust formation, perceived humanness, social influence, and adoption of generative AI and LLMs.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological transformation
themes.description: Papers investigate LLMs as analytical collaborators, data classifiers, and research instruments, emphasizing validation, transparency, and governance.

themes.name: AI in education and learning
themes.description: Research investigates AI-enabled pedagogy, student engagement, AI literacy development, and collaborative learning with teachers and AI across K-12 and higher education.

themes.name: AI in health and wellbeing: information quality and instruction
themes.description: A cluster analyzes AI-mediated health misinformation, patient education, and digital health governance, with attention to safety, readability, and equity.
